To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the appropriate sampling frequency for diatom-based river monitoring depends on the season and catchment wetness conditions.
(1) sampling frequency is a key factor for diatom-based bio-monitoring, and (2) sampling intervals need to be reduced with increasing wetness conditions.

(i) sampling frequency should be reduced in wet seasons and increased in dry seasons; (ii) sampling frequency should also be adjusted to the catchment hydrological wetness; (iii) sampling frequency should vary with the temporal dynamics of diatom communities; and (iv) sampling frequency should not be constant throughout the year.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach for determining ASFs of riverine diatoms and its application in a lowland river.
how to capture diatom temporal dynamics with a specific sampling frequency.
a better understanding of the temporal dynamics of freshwater diatom assemblages and their implications on the development of bio-monitoring protocols.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ASF should be adjusted according to the season, catchment conditions and the specific diatom assemblage.
diatom bio-monitoring protocols must be developed in a way to capture diatom temporal dynamics with a suitable sampling frequency.
the ASF is highly variable over space and time, and is related to the hydrology of the river system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
diatom bio-assessment should be conducted at least twice a week when the catchment is wet and once a month when the catchment becomes dry.
the ASF of a riverine diatom community is highly dynamic and can change over a short period of time.
a sampling frequency should be adjusted to capture the temporal variation in diatom community composition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ASFs of diatoms can be estimated with the SOM method, and that the ASF is a function of the hydrological condition of the catchment.
diatom-based bioassessment should be carried out with an appropriate sampling interval to avoid false conclusions.
diatom sampling frequency can be reduced in the wet season but increased in the dry season.
